title: Minimum Wage Australia 16 Year-Old: Hourly to Annual Pay Guide
description: Learn how the minimum wage in Australia applies to 16-year-olds. Convert hourly rates to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay with tax and super estimates.
salarySummary: For a 16-year-old on the junior minimum wage rate, the annual gross pay is calculated by multiplying the hourly rate by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks, then adding super on top.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage in Australia for a 16-year-old?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage for adults is $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. However, junior rates apply to employees under 21, including 16-year-olds. The exact percentage of the adult rate depends on the award or agreement. For example, under the Miscellaneous Award, a 16-year-old might receive 45–50% of the adult rate. Check the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides for your specific industry.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual pay from an hourly rate if I’m a casual 16-year-old worker?
faqs.a: If you are a casual employee, your base hourly rate should not already include casual loading. On our timesheet, you enter the base rate and tick the 25% casual loading checkbox. Then multiply that loaded rate by hours per week (usually 38 for full-time) and 52 weeks to get annual gross. For example, a base rate of $13.22/hour (approx 50% of adult minimum) becomes $16.53/hour with loading, giving an annual gross of about $32,660 before tax and super.

faqs.q: Does a 16-year-old pay tax and Medicare on their earnings?
faqs.a: Yes, if your annual income exceeds the tax-free threshold of $18,200, you pay resident tax at progressive rates (15% up to $45,000, etc.) plus the Medicare levy of 2%. For a 16-year-old earning under $18,200, no tax is withheld, but you may still need to lodge a return. Super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% by your employer, up to the maximum contribution base.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Minimum Wage in Australia for a 16-Year-Old

If you are a 16-year-old working in Australia, your pay is likely governed by the National Minimum Wage or an award rate. The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage, which from 1 July 2026 is **$26.44 per hour** for adult employees not covered by an award. However, junior rates apply to workers under 21, including 16-year-olds. These rates are a percentage of the adult minimum wage and vary by age and industry. For example, under many awards, a 16-year-old might receive 45–50% of the adult rate. Always check the relevant [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Ombudsman for your exact entitlement.

### How to Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

The standard formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For a full-time employee, we assume 38 hours per week (the ordinary hours under the National Employment Standards). If you work part-time or casual, use your actual weekly hours. For example, a 16-year-old on a junior rate of $13.22 per hour (50% of adult minimum) working 38 hours per week would earn:

- Weekly gross: $13.22 × 38 = $502.36
- Fortnightly gross: $502.36 × 2 = $1,004.72
- Annual gross: $13.22 × 38 × 52 = $26,122.72

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. On our [timesheet](/), you enter the base hourly rate (without loading) and tick the checkbox to add 25%. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. The calculator then applies the loading automatically.

### Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Income above that is taxed at:

- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For a 16-year-old earning $26,122.72 (from the example above), tax would be approximately ($26,122.72 – $18,200) × 15% = $1,188.41, plus Medicare levy of $522.45, giving total deductions of about $1,710.86. Your annual take-home would be around $24,411.86. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed estimate.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of **12%** of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay—it’s an extra amount paid into a super fund. The super guarantee applies up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a 16-year-old earning $26,122.72, the super contribution would be $3,134.73 per year. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor, but many industries have award rates that are higher. Awards also specify junior rates, casual loadings, penalty rates, and allowances. If you are covered by an award, your minimum pay is the award rate, not the National Minimum Wage. Always check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website or use our [reference tables](/data) to find your correct rate.

### Casual Loading Explained

Casual employees receive a 25% loading to compensate for not receiving paid leave (sick leave, annual leave). The loading is applied to the base hourly rate. For a 16-year-old casual, the base junior rate (e.g., $13.22) becomes $16.53 per hour with loading. This loaded rate is then used in the annual calculation. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how it works.

### Average Pay Comparisons

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time as $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). This is an average, not a median, and includes adults only. For all employees (including part-time), the average is $1,579.20 per week. A 16-year-old’s earnings will typically be much lower due to junior rates and fewer hours. See our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more context.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a quick calculation, visit our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page or use the [timesheet](/).
